comments.text: Why is Damascus an oasis? I never understood it. In the 2nd Crusade, the crusaders led by German king Conrad III and French king Louis VII arrived to besiege Damascus. They came from the west. There were lush gardens, The soldiers pick fruit, water was plentiful. But the city did not fall right away. Impatient, the leaders are fed misinformation that the walls of the city are easier to take from the southeast. The walls there hold, but there is no food or water for the troops. Approaching Muslim troops are on the march. The crusaders are in a trap. On 28 July, 1148 the order for retreat is given.  Your exposition at the beginning of the video, about the snows of the Anti-Lebanon to the west of Damascus and water from the melting snow flowing into the River Barada then being diverted into myriads of smaller channels, explains everything. An Aha moment explaning the microgeography of Damascus and the historical event mentioned.  Thank you for the marvelous video. Let us pray that the new government in Syria is effective and fair, that Syria can heal and that those who fled can return to live again in their homeland.
